name: accuracy.assess
doc: The accuracy and the area of a map's classes from a stratified random sample labelled with the reference class (Olofsson et al. 2014): the error matrix in shares of the area, the user's, producer's and overall accuracies, and each class's area estimated from the sample instead of counted on the map, with standard errors and confidence intervals; as R's mapaccuracy: olofsson when the strata are the map's classes, stehman2014 for strata of their own (a map of strata, or the finite population correction).

inputs.name: map
inputs.doc: the classified map: its class at each point and its cells by class

inputs.name: points
inputs.doc: the sample's points with their reference class (accuracy.sample's, labelled)

inputs.name: samples
inputs.doc: the sample as a table instead: columns map and reference (and stratum, with strata)

inputs.name: strata
inputs.doc: the strata of the sample when they are not the map's classes (e.g. an older map, or a buffer around change)

outputs.name: table
outputs.doc: a row per class: class, map_cells, samples, user_accuracy, user_se, user_ci, producer_accuracy, producer_se, producer_ci, area_share, area_share_se, area_cells, area_cells_ci, area_ha, area_ha_ci (the _ci the half-widths of the confidence intervals)

outputs.name: overall
outputs.doc: overall_accuracy, overall_se, overall_ci, samples, cells, confidence

outputs.name: matrix
outputs.doc: the error matrix in shares of the area: a row per class of the map, a column per reference class

outputs.name: counts
outputs.doc: the error matrix in sample units

params.name: reference
params.doc: the column of the reference class (default reference)

params.name: estimator
params.doc: olofsson (the strata are the map's classes), stehman (strata of their own, the finite population correction); auto (default): stehman with strata, else olofsson

params.name: confidence
params.doc: the level of the confidence intervals (default 0.95)

params.name: cell_area
params.doc: a cell's area in m2 (default: the cells' sides)

name: accuracy.sample
doc: A stratified random sample of a map's cells for its accuracy and area (Olofsson et al. 2014): in every stratum its share of cells drawn without replacement, as numpy's default_rng(seed).choice of the stratum's cells, stratum after stratum (increasing); the points at the cells' centres, by stratum and cell. Give each point its reference class (the column reference, from imagery or the field) and take them to accuracy.assess.

inputs.name: map
inputs.doc: the strata: the classified map, or a map of strata

inputs.name: sizes
inputs.doc: the sample of each stratum: columns stratum and n (accuracy.sample_size's table)

outputs.name: points
outputs.doc: the points: id, stratum, row, col, x, y and reference (empty, to be filled)

outputs.name: cells
outputs.doc: the stratum of the cells drawn, missing elsewhere

params.name: n
params.doc: the sample of each stratum instead of sizes: a number for all, or {stratum: n}

params.name: seed
params.doc: the seed of numpy's generator (default 1)

name: accuracy.sample_size
doc: The size of a stratified random sample for the accuracy and the area of a map, and its share of each stratum (Olofsson et al. 2014): n = (Σ W_i S_i / S(Ô))², W_i a stratum's share of the map, S_i = √(U_i (1 − U_i)) from the user's accuracy expected of it, S(Ô) the standard error wanted of the overall accuracy. Shared with a minimum in every stratum (the good practice when some classes are rare, such as change: the rest in proportion to the areas), in proportion, equally or by Neyman's allocation.

inputs.name: map
inputs.doc: the strata: the classified map, or a map of strata

outputs.name: table
outputs.doc: a row per stratum: stratum, cells, weight, user_accuracy, sd, n

outputs.name: n
outputs.doc: the size of the sample

params.name: user_accuracy
params.doc: the user's accuracy expected of each stratum: a number for all (default 0.9), or {class: accuracy} (the others 0.9); lower for the classes hard to map, such as change (Olofsson's 0.6 to 0.7)

params.name: standard_error
params.doc: the standard error wanted of the overall accuracy (default 0.01)

params.name: n
params.doc: the size of the sample, instead of the formula's

params.name: allocation
params.doc: how the sample is shared among the strata (default minimum)

params.name: minimum
params.doc: the sample of every stratum at least, or all its cells (allocation minimum; default 50; Olofsson suggests 50 to 100)

name: batch.run
doc: An operator run on many rasters in parallel (landschaft's batch, GuidosToolbox's Batch Process): each worker reads one raster, runs the operator on it and writes what it gives to the output folder, named after the input and the operator: maps <name>_<operator>[_<output>].tif, tables .csv, texts .txt, and <name>_<operator>.json with the parameters, the files, the numbers and the time (an input whose JSON exists is skipped unless overwrite). MSPA with GuidosToolbox's naming. A row per input: ok, skipped (done before), seconds, files written; the errors in the report. A folder given to any node that takes a map does the same, its maps seen and its settings in its pane (Make it a chain of nodes, in the app).

doc: Logistic regression of the presence of each class on the drivers (lulcc's glmModels, R's glm.fit operation for operation), on the cells with a value in the map and in the class's drivers.

inputs.name: drivers

name: glm.predict

inputs.name: landscape
inputs.doc: a map whose missing cells stay missing

outputs.name: suitability
outputs.doc: a layer per class

name: hydro.along_network
doc: The stretches of river up and down from every point within a distance along the network, as hydrographr's get_buffer_along_the_network: downstream along the D8 directions, upstream along every stream that flows into it (a buffer that follows the river, not a circle: the reach of a fish, of a spill below a mine). Each cell given the point nearest to it along the network.

inputs.name: points

inputs.name: streams

outputs.name: distance

name: hydro.breach
doc: Remove the depressions of a DEM by cutting channels through their rims (least-cost breaching, WhiteboxTools' BreachDepressionsLeastCost after Lindsay & Dhun 2015): each pit, from the lowest, joined to the nearest cell it can drain to by the channel of least cost; often changes the terrain less than filling.

inputs.name: dem

outputs.name: map
outputs.doc: the breached DEM

params.name: max_cost

params.name: min_dist

params.name: flat_increment
params.doc: the drop per cell along a channel (default: from the elevations, as WhiteboxTools)

params.name: fill_rest
params.doc: fill the depressions no channel could solve (default true)

name: hydro.centrality
doc: The place of every link in its river network, as hydrographr's get_centrality on the graph of the links: the links flowing into it, its degree, its Shreve magnitude (the sources above it), the length of river above it, and its betweenness (the pairs of links whose path goes through it) and closeness (one over the sum of the steps to every other link of its network), igraph's on the undirected graph.

inputs.name: links
inputs.doc: the links' table of hydro.stream_links (link, downstream, length)

outputs.name: table
outputs.doc: link, downstream, upstream, degree, magnitude, upstream_length, betweenness, closeness

name: hydro.connectivity_index
doc: The index of connectivity (Borselli et al. 2008) as InVEST's sediment delivery ratio model computes it: log10 of the upslope over the downslope component, the weight (a land use's USLE C) and pygeoprocessing's slope along its routing; no value on the streams.

inputs.doc: the elevations (no value: missing), best with depressions filled

inputs.name: weight

inputs.name: streams
inputs.doc: 1 on the streams (else from the threshold)

outputs.name: map
outputs.doc: the index

params.name: threshold
params.doc: the flow accumulation (cells) of a stream, without streams

params.name: method
params.doc: the routing: mfd (default) or d8

name: hydro.dci
doc: The dendritic connectivity index of a river network cut by barriers (Cote et al. 2009), as R's riverconn: the network split into segments at each dam, weir or culvert, each segment weighted by its length (or its habitat); the potamodromous DCI (the chance that a fish can swim between two points of the river, 0 to 100) and the diadromous one (between the mouth and a point), from the passability of each barrier up and down. For every barrier, the DCI if it were removed and its gain (riverconn's d_index, percent): which dams to remove first.

inputs.name: barriers
inputs.doc: the barriers as points, moved onto the streams; their passability from the attributes pass_u and pass_d, or passability (0 to 1)

inputs.name: weights
inputs.doc: the habitat of each cell: a segment weighs the length of its cells times this (default 1)

outputs.name: table
outputs.doc: a row per network with barriers: network (its mouth segment), segments, barriers, weight, dci_p, dci_d

outputs.name: barriers
outputs.doc: the barriers moved, their attributes and segment, network, pass_u, pass_d, dci_p_removed, d_index (the percent the DCI of its network grows when it is removed), rank (1 the largest)

outputs.name: segments
outputs.doc: the segment of each stream cell (1..), 0 elsewhere

outputs.name: reach
outputs.doc: on each stream cell, riverconn's reach index of its segment, 0 to 100: the share of its network a fish there can reach

params.name: flats
params.doc: drain flat areas towards lower terrain and away from higher terrain (Barnes et al. 2014; default true)

params.name: passability
params.doc: of the barriers without pass_u, pass_d or passability attributes (0: impassable)

params.name: direction
params.doc: symmetric (default: the product of the passabilities up and down at every barrier, Cote's) or asymmetric (up through a barrier going upstream, down going downstream)

params.name: snap
params.doc: the largest move of a barrier onto the streams, map units (300 m; 3 cells without a projection)

name: hydro.distance_to_channel

inputs.doc: the elevations (no value: missing), best with depressions filled

inputs.name: streams

inputs.name: weights

outputs.name: map
outputs.doc: the distance

name: hydro.fill
doc: Fill the depressions of a DEM so that water flows from every cell to the edge: each depression raised to where it would spill over (Priority-Flood, Barnes, Lehman & Mulla 2014; the DEM of WhiteboxTools' FillDepressions), through landschaft's C++.

outputs.name: map

name: hydro.flow_accumulation
doc: The area that drains through each cell (itself included): all to the steepest neighbour (d8), split between the two cells of the D-infinity azimuth (dinf), among the lower neighbours by slope^exponent (fd8, Freeman 1991) or by slope times contour length (quinn, Quinn et al. 1991), or pygeoprocessing's multiple flow directions (mfd, the InVEST models'). WhiteboxTools' accumulations cell for cell.

inputs.name: dem
inputs.doc: the elevations (no value: missing), best with depressions filled

inputs.doc: the elevations (no value: missing), best with depressions filled

outputs.name: map

params.name: flats
params.doc: drain flat areas towards lower terrain and away from higher terrain (Barnes et al. 2014; default true)

inputs.name: streams

params.doc: drain flat areas towards lower terrain and away from higher terrain (Barnes et al. 2014; default true)

params.name: snap

doc: Points moved onto the stream network, as hydrographr's snap_to_network: gauges, dams, records of fish each to the centre of the nearest stream cell within a distance (of equally near ones the first in raster order), or of the nearest whose flow accumulation is at least a minimum (on the river, not a tributary beside it). doc: The correlation and the least squares line between two maps in a moving window around every cell (geographically local regression, as terra's focalPairs or focalReg): Pearson's correlation, the slope and intercept of y on x and r², over the cells of the window where both have a value. name: raster.majority
doc: A map of classes cleaned by the majority filter, as ArcGIS's Majority Filter: a cell takes the most common class of its neighbours (with a value) when more than half of them hold it (`replace` majority) or at least half (half); a tie between classes keeps the cell. name: raster.match
doc: Rasters on the grid of another (its CRS, extent and cells: landschaft's match_grid, by gdalwarp), so that their cells are the same cells; the method by the data unless one is given.

doc: A raster: a file, or a folder or a pattern (forest/*.tif) for every raster in it as one stack (a layer per band of each file, by the files' names; files of different grids are shown, and made one grid by raster.match before they are a stack). doc: A map's values changed by rules, one per line: `1 2 3 -> 1` (values), `0..10 -> 2` (a range, both ends in; also written `0 10 2`, from, to, becomes), `* -> nan` (every other value); values no rule takes stay as they are. The first rule that takes a value gives it.

doc: The patches smaller than a size merged into their largest neighbour, as gdal_sieve (GDALSieveFilter): a map of classes rid of its specks, the smallest patches first, each taking the value of the largest patch it touches (a patch grown by the merge counts as its new size). name: raster.standardize
doc: A map (or every layer of a stack, or every map of a series) put on a common scale, for drivers and predictors compared or combined: the z-score ((x - mean) / std, the std of the population), min-max to 0-1, or the percentile stretch to 0-1 between two percentiles (the values beyond them 0 or 1). outputs.name: table
outputs.doc: a row per layer (1.., in the stack's order): its statistics

params.doc:

outputs.doc: the measure

params.name: options

params.name: path
params.doc: the file (or folder, for a series) made; else a cache

params.name: anthropic

params.name: failsafe
params.doc: the natural classes the failsafe fills (default all)

params.name: threshold
params.doc: the share of land a source must explain (default 0.95)

params.name: restore_to
params.doc: original (default) or current: restored land returns to the current natural cover where it has some

name: restoration.plan
doc: Restoration planning (Strassburg et al. 2020): how much of every converted cell to restore for the most benefit within area targets and a budget: the reduction of the species' extinction risk (the species-area relationship on their area of habitat, sdm.area_of_habitat's table and gain) and linear benefits (carbon per km²). exact: the optimum within a tolerance (simplicial decomposition with a proven bound); steps: Strassburg et al.'s procedure (the target in steps, the benefits recomputed between them); uniform: every cell by the same share.

inputs.name: restorable
inputs.doc: the share of every cell that can be restored (anthropic land)

inputs.name: conservable
inputs.doc: the share of every cell's natural land conservation can keep (C): without the plan, threat of it is lost

inputs.name: convertible
inputs.doc: the share of every cell's natural land that can be converted (D; with restorable, R + D)

inputs.name: threat
inputs.doc: conservation: the share of the conservable land lost without it (1)

inputs.name: loss
inputs.doc: sdm.area_of_habitat's loss (conservation, conversion)

inputs.name: table
inputs.doc: sdm.area_of_habitat's table: current, potential, valid

inputs.name: gain
inputs.doc: sdm.area_of_habitat's gain: habitat per unit of a cell restored

inputs.name: linear
inputs.doc: linear benefits per km² restored (carbon...), a layer each

inputs.name: cost
inputs.doc: the cost per km² restored (with budget)

inputs.name: regions
inputs.doc: region codes, for targets per region

inputs.name: limit
inputs.doc: the bound limit: a share per cell multiplying the restorable

inputs.name: hfi
inputs.doc: the human footprint, for the intactness benefit

inputs.name: reduction
inputs.doc: intactness: the footprint a cell loses per unit restored

inputs.name: increase
inputs.doc: intactness: the footprint a cell gains per unit of natural land converted (or lost unconserved)

outputs.name: restored
outputs.doc: the share of every cell restored

outputs.name: conserved
outputs.doc: the share of every cell's natural land conserved

outputs.name: converted
outputs.doc: the share of every cell's natural land converted

outputs.name: summary
outputs.doc: the weighted benefit, the area (km²), the cost, the bound (exact), optimal (1), the rounds, the extinction risk's reduction and its standard deviation

outputs.name: tradeoff
outputs.doc: with levels: per level its share, the landscape target, the area and the weighted benefit

outputs.name: gradient
outputs.doc: with levels: the levels whose plan acts on the cell (conversion: the levels plus one less that)

outputs.name: benefits
outputs.doc: per benefit (the risk, the linear ones, intactness): value, weight, weighted

outputs.name: weights
outputs.doc: with weights: per set the weights (w.<benefit>), the benefits, the cost, and Strassburg et al.'s mean, sd, score and rank

outputs.name: species
outputs.doc: per species counted (its row in the area of habitat's table): the habitat gained, the risk without and with the plan, the reduction

params.name: method
params.doc: exact (default), steps or uniform

params.name: levels
params.doc: a trade-off curve: the landscape target's shares at every level (increasing, in (0, 1])

params.name: nested
params.doc: exact trade-offs: every level contains the previous (true)

params.name: threshold
params.doc: the gradient: a cell counts when its share is above (0)

params.name: projected_change
params.doc: projected changes of natural land per region ({code: km²}; + spared for restoration, - demanded)

params.name: change_sense
params.doc: the projected changes' rows (= default)

params.name: restrict
params.doc: restore and convert: every region in its direction only (true)

params.name: compensate
params.doc: restore only: the land demanded elsewhere taken from it (true)

params.name: steps
params.doc: steps: the parts of the target (default 1)

params.name: target
params.doc: the area restored (km²): a number for the landscape, or {region code: area} with regions

params.name: sense
params.doc: the targets' sense: <= (default, at most), >=, =

params.name: relative
params.doc: the targets are shares of the area that can be restored

params.name: budget
params.doc: the most the plan may cost (with cost)

params.name: z
params.doc: the species-area exponent: a number (0.25) or one per species

params.name: weight
params.doc: the risk benefit's weight (1)

params.name: linear_weights
params.doc: the linear benefits' weights (1 each)

params.name: restoration_discount
params.doc: the share of the habitat value restored land does not deliver (0; one or one per species)

params.name: cell_area
params.doc: a cell's area in km² (default: the grid's)

params.name: z_sd
params.doc: the standard deviation of z (0.1 in Strassburg et al. 2020; one or one per species counted): the risk reduction's

params.name: uncertainty
params.doc: how the species' sensitivities to z add up: correlated (default), independent or linear (Strassburg et al.'s)

params.name: intactness_weight
params.doc: the intactness benefit's weight (1; with hfi)

params.name: intactness_form
params.doc: linear (default: its gradient at the plan of nothing, recomputed between steps) or exact (the total intactness)

params.name: radius
params.doc: intactness: the neighbourhood's radius in cells (3)

params.name: gamma
params.doc: intactness: the footprint's decay of quality (-ln(0.2)/4)

params.name: beta
params.doc: intactness: the distance's decay per km (-0.2)

params.name: intactness_z
params.doc: intactness: the exponent of the pairs' quality (0.5)

params.name: cell_size
params.doc: intactness: a cell's size in km, or [width, height] (default: the grid's, projected)

params.name: min_benefit
params.doc: the cheapest plan whose weighted benefit reaches this (with cost; exact)

params.name: weights
params.doc: sets of weights to compare ([{benefit: weight}]; the benefits extinction_risk, the linear layers' names, intactness): the plan of the best ranked

params.name: tolerance
params.doc: exact: the relative gap to the bound (1e-7)

params.name: time_limit
params.doc: exact: seconds (default none)

name: restoration.resistance
doc: A resistance growing with the distance to the habitat, as GuidosToolbox's Setup Tools -> Distance -> Resistance (landschaft's distance_to_resistance): the background round(distance + 2) up to 100 (3 next to the habitat), the habitat 2, missing 0; IDL's quasi-Euclidean distance.

inputs.name: map
inputs.doc: the map (0 missing, 1 background, 2 habitat)

outputs.name: map
outputs.doc: the resistance

params.name: foreground
params.doc: the foreground's classes (a class or a list)

name: restoration.status
doc: How connected the habitat is and how much reconnecting it could add, as GuidosToolbox's Restoration Status (landschaft's restoration_status): the habitat's objects (8-connected), the equivalent connected area ECA = sqrt(sum of their areas squared), the coherence ECA / habitat (%), the restoration potential (100 - coherence), the habitat's share of the area with data (RAC), the average patch size and the critical new object area.

inputs.name: map
inputs.doc: the habitat map (0 missing, 1 background, 2 habitat)

outputs.name: stats
outputs.doc: the area with data, objects, habitat, largest object, APS, CNOA, ECA, coherence (%), restoration potential (%), RAC (%)

params.name: foreground
params.doc: the foreground's classes (a class or a list)

name: rng.numpy

inputs.name: seed
inputs.doc: the seed (taken modulo 2^32)

outputs.name: rng
outputs.doc: the generator

name: rng.r
doc: R's random number generator after set.seed(seed) (Mersenne-Twister), as lulcc and landschaft use it: carry it along a loop so that every step draws after the previous one.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.doc: the seed

outputs.name: rng
outputs.doc: the generator

name: sdm.accessible_area
doc: The area the species could have reached, where its background is drawn (landschaft's accessible_area, the M of the BAM diagram): the land within a distance of the records (geodesic circles, merged), their convex hull or the regions that hold them (widened by the distance if given), cut at the antimeridian, within a mask.

inputs.name: occurrences
inputs.doc: points, or a table with coordinate columns

inputs.name: regions
inputs.doc: polygons (ecoregions, biomes...), for regions

inputs.name: within
inputs.doc: polygons the area is cut to

outputs.name: area
outputs.doc: one (multi)polygon in lon/lat

params.name: x
params.doc: the table's x column (default x, lon, longitude...)

params.name: y
params.doc: the table's y column (default y, lat, latitude...)

params.name: method
params.doc: buffer (default), convex_hull or regions

params.name: distance
params.doc: the radius in metres (required for buffer)

params.name: resolution
params.doc: the vertices of each circle (default 64)

name: sdm.area_of_habitat
doc: The area of habitat of species (Brooks et al. 2019; Strassburg et al. 2020): over the cells of each species' range (within its elevation limits), the shares of the natural classes suitable to it times the cell's area, now and before conversion (the original vegetation); and the habitat it gains per unit of a cell restored. Rows in the order of the ranges' layers.

inputs.name: ranges
inputs.doc: each species' range (cells above 0), by species

inputs.name: land_cover
inputs.doc: the share of each class, by name

inputs.name: original
inputs.doc: the original share of each natural class

inputs.name: restore
inputs.doc: the shares restored land returns to

inputs.name: anthropic
inputs.doc: the share of anthropic land (where restoring gains)

inputs.name: elevation
inputs.doc: the elevation, for the species' limits

outputs.name: table
outputs.doc: per species (in the ranges' order): its area of habitat now and potential (km²), its range's cells, and whether it counts (1: habitat now and potential, and suitable classes)

outputs.name: gain
outputs.doc: the habitat each species gains per unit of a cell restored

outputs.name: loss
outputs.doc: with loss: the habitat each species loses per unit of a cell's natural land converted

params.name: natural
params.doc: the natural classes (names of the land cover's layers)

params.name: suitability
params.doc: each species' suitable classes: {species: [classes]} (the species not listed: every natural class)

params.name: include_unlisted
params.doc: species not in suitability count (default true)

params.name: elevation_limits
params.doc: [[species, lowest, highest], ...] (null: none)

params.name: cell_area
params.doc: a cell's area in km² (default: the grid's)

params.name: loss
params.doc: also the habitat lost per unit of natural land (conservation, conversion)

name: sdm.autocorrelation_range
doc: The range of spatial autocorrelation of the predictors (landschaft's autocorrelation_range, blockCV's cv_spatial_autocor): gstat's variograms (spherical, exponential, Gaussian and Matern) fitted to a sample of every layer, the best one's range; their median and the block size it gives for spatial blocks.

inputs.name: env
inputs.doc: the predictors: a stack or a map

outputs.name: range
outputs.doc: the median range (metres on lon/lat grids)

outputs.name: block_size
outputs.doc: the size of spatial blocks (degrees on lon/lat grids)

outputs.name: layers
outputs.doc: per layer: range, sill, nugget, kappa

outputs.name: models
outputs.doc: per layer, the variogram model

params.name: n
params.doc: the cells sampled per layer (default 5000)

params.name: seed
params.doc: the seed of R's generator (default 1)

params.name: deg_to_metre
params.doc: metres per degree on lon/lat (111325)

name: sdm.background
doc: Background points for a species distribution model (landschaft's background, dismo's randomPoints): cells with values in every predictor drawn with R's sampling (weighted by the cells' widths on lon/lat grids, or by a bias), within an area, a band of distances from the records or outside their environmental envelope, the records' cells left out.

inputs.name: env
inputs.doc: the predictors: a stack or a map

inputs.name: occurrences
inputs.doc: the records (points or a table)

inputs.name: area
inputs.doc: the area to draw within

inputs.name: bias
inputs.doc: a weight per cell

outputs.name: points
outputs.doc: the points at the cells' centres, with their cell

params.name: x
params.doc: the table's x column (default x, lon, longitude...)

params.name: y
params.doc: the table's y column (default y, lat, latitude...)

params.name: n
params.doc: the points (default 10000)

params.name: distance
params.doc: the largest distance from the records, or [from, to]

params.name: envelope
params.doc: outside the records' quantiles [q, 1 - q] of every predictor

params.name: exclude_occurrences
params.doc: leave the records' cells out (default true)

params.name: tryf
params.doc: the candidates drawn per point (default 3)

params.name: lonlat_correction
params.doc: weight lon/lat cells by their width (default true)

params.name: seed
params.doc: the seed of R's generator (default 1)

name: sdm.bias_surface
doc: The sampling effort as a surface (landschaft's bias_surface): a Gaussian kernel density of the records of a whole group (the same taxa, collectors and decades) on the grid of the predictors, MASS::kde2d's at the cells' centres, with R's bw.nrd in each direction by default. The bias of sdm.background, which draws the background with the records' bias (a target-group background, Phillips et al. 2009; Maxent's bias file). kde2d(h = H) is bandwidth = H / 4.

inputs.name: occurrences
inputs.doc: the records of the target group: points, or a table with coordinate columns

inputs.name: env
inputs.doc: the predictors: a stack or a map (its grid)

outputs.name: bias
outputs.doc: the density (the share of the records per unit of area of the coordinate system: it sums to 1 over the plane) or rescaled

outputs.name: bandwidth
outputs.doc: the bandwidths used, [x, y]

params.name: x
params.doc: the table's x column (default x, lon, longitude...)

params.name: y
params.doc: the table's y column (default y, lat, latitude...)

params.name: bandwidth
params.doc: the kernel's standard deviation in the grid's units (metres, or degrees on lon/lat): a number, [x, y], or nrd (default: R's bw.nrd in each direction, kde2d's)

params.name: isotropic
params.doc: the larger bandwidth in both directions (default false)

params.name: limits
params.doc: [min, max]: bandwidths raised or lowered to them (either null); a floor keeps a clustered group's surface from collapsing on its records

params.name: weights
params.doc: a column of the records: each one's weight (specimens, visits); default 1

params.name: rescale
params.doc: [lo, hi]: the densities mapped linearly to them, e.g. [0.05, 0.95], so that every cell keeps a chance

params.name: mask
params.doc: no value on the cells without a value in every predictor (default true)

name: sdm.boyce
doc: The continuous Boyce index (landschaft's boyce, ecospat's ecospat.boyce): the correlation between the classes of suitability and their ratio of predicted to expected presences, in a moving window (default) or in classes.

inputs.name: presences
inputs.doc: the predictions at the presences

inputs.name: available
inputs.doc: the predictions everywhere (or at the background and the presences)

outputs.name: cor
outputs.doc: the index (rounded to 3 digits)

outputs.name: table
outputs.doc: the classes: f_ratio, hs, used

params.name: column

params.name: nclass

params.name: window
params.doc: the window's width (default a tenth of the range)

params.name: res
params.doc: the window's steps (default 100)

params.name: method
params.doc: spearman (default), pearson or kendall

params.name: rm_duplicate
params.doc: drop repeated ratios (default true)

name: sdm.buffer_folds

outputs.name: folds
outputs.doc: per fold the records (0-based) to train and to test on

name: sdm.checkerboard_folds

inputs.name: env

outputs.name: records
outputs.doc: the records with their fold

params.name: presence
params.doc: their presence column, 1 or 0 (default presence)

params.name: x
params.doc: the table's x column

params.name: y
params.doc: the table's y column

params.name: aggregation
params.doc: the factor (default 2), or two

name: sdm.clean_occurrences
doc: Occurrence records with suspicious coordinates flagged or dropped (landschaft's clean_occurrences, CoordinateCleaner's tests): invalid coordinates, equal longitude and latitude, 0/0, capitals, country and province centroids, the sea, towns, outside the country they claim, geographic outliers of their species, GBIF's headquarters, biodiversity institutions, duplicates and artificial hotspots. Each test takes false (skip it), true (its defaults), a number (its main option) or an object of its options. CoordinateCleaner's tables travel with Terraflux; Natural Earth's land, urban areas and countries are downloaded on first use (or connect your own).

inputs.name: occurrences
inputs.doc: points, or a table with coordinate columns

inputs.name: capitals_ref
inputs.doc: capitals in place of CoordinateCleaner's (points)

inputs.name: centroids_ref
inputs.doc: centroids in place of CoordinateCleaner's (points)

inputs.name: institutions_ref
inputs.doc: institutions in place of CoordinateCleaner's (points)

inputs.name: seas_ref
inputs.doc: the land, in place of Natural Earth's (polygons)

inputs.name: urban_ref
inputs.doc: urban areas in place of Natural Earth's

inputs.name: countries_ref
inputs.doc: countries in place of Natural Earth's

outputs.name: occurrences
outputs.doc: the records that pass every test, or (flag) all with flag_<test> and flagged

outputs.name: counts

params.doc: the table's x column (default x, lon, longitude...)

params.name: y
params.doc: the table's y column (default y, lat, latitude...)

params.name: species
params.doc: the column of the species (default species, scientificName or label)

params.name: action
params.doc: drop (default) or flag the suspicious records

params.name: equal
params.doc: equal longitude and latitude (default true)

params.name: zeros
params.doc: at 0/0: buffer, degrees around 0/0 (default 0.5)

params.name: capitals
params.doc: at a country's capital: buffer (metres, default 10000), geod (true), verify (false)

params.name: centroids
params.doc: at a country's or province's centroid: buffer (metres, default 1000), detail (both, country or provinces), geod (true), verify (false)

params.name: seas
params.doc: in the sea: scale of Natural Earth's land (110, 50 or 10; default 50)

params.name: urban
params.doc: in Natural Earth's urban areas (default false)

params.name: countries
params.doc: outside the country it claims: column (the records' ISO codes; a text sets it), ref_col (default iso_a2_eh for two-letter codes, else iso_a3_eh); default false

params.name: outliers
params.doc: far from the records of its species: method (quantile, mad or distance), mltpl (5), tdi (km, 1000), size (7), min_occs (7), thinning (false), thinning_res (0.5)

params.name: gbif

params.name: duplicates

params.name: aohi

inputs.name: background

inputs.name: env
inputs.doc: the predictors: a stack (by name) or a map

outputs.name: records

inputs.name: background

outputs.name: table

outputs.name: boyce

doc: Mesgaran's extrapolation detection (landschaft's exdet): NT1, below 0 where a predictor falls outside the reference's range, and inside the ranges NT2, the Mahalanobis distance against the reference's largest (above 1 a novel combination); mic, the most influential covariate, by its 1-based place among the predictors (0: no novelty).

params.name: type

params.name: clamp

params.name: model

params.name: n_estimators

params.name: min_samples_split
params.doc: random_forest: default 2

params.name: max_depth

params.name: max_features

Usually of a surface with its trend removed. A table of one row.

inputs.name: map
inputs.doc: the surface (no value: missing)

outputs.name: table
outputs.doc: a column per metric

params.name: metrics
params.doc: names (sa, sq, sku, sdr, sal...; default every one)

name: surface.peaks
doc: The peaks (or valleys) of a surface, geodiv's findpeaks: the cells higher (lower) than their 8 neighbours; a table of their centres, values, rows and columns.

inputs.name: map
inputs.doc: the surface (an elevation...)

outputs.name: table
outputs.doc: x, y, value, row, col

params.name: valleys
params.doc: the valleys instead

name: surface.spherical_sd
doc: The spherical standard deviation of the surface's normals in a window (spatialEco's spherical.sd), or their variance.

inputs.name: map
inputs.doc: the surface (an elevation...)

outputs.name: map
outputs.doc: the spherical standard deviation

params.name: d
params.doc: the window: odd cells, or [rows, columns] (3)

params.name: variance
params.doc: the variance instead

name: surface.srr
doc: The surface relief ratio (spatialEco's srr): (mean - min) / (max - min) in a window.

inputs.name: map
inputs.doc: the surface (an elevation...)

outputs.name: map
outputs.doc: the SRR

params.name: s
params.doc: the window: odd cells, or [rows, columns] (5)

name: surface.terrain
doc: Slope or aspect of a surface as terra::terrain (Horn's 8 or 4 neighbours), through landschaft's C++; no value on the edge cells.

inputs.name: map
inputs.doc: the surface (an elevation...)

outputs.name: map
outputs.doc: the slope or aspect

params.name: v
params.doc: slope (default) or aspect

params.name: unit
params.doc: degrees (default) or radians

params.name: neighbors
params.doc: 8 (default) or 4

name: surface.tpi
doc: The topographic position index (spatialEco's tpi): each cell's value less the mean of a window around it (a rectangle of cells, or a circle of a radius in map units).

inputs.name: map
inputs.doc: the surface (an elevation...)

outputs.name: map
outputs.doc: the TPI

params.name: scale
params.doc: the window: odd cells, or a circle's radius (3)

params.name: win
params.doc: rectangle (default) or circle

params.name: normalize
params.doc: divided by the window's standard deviation

name: surface.trasp
doc: The transformed aspect (spatialEco's trasp): (1 - cos(aspect - 30°)) / 2, from 0 (north-northeast) to 1.

inputs.name: map
inputs.doc: the surface (an elevation...)

outputs.name: map
outputs.doc: the TRASP

name: surface.tri
doc: The terrain ruggedness index (spatialEco's tri) in an odd window of cells.

inputs.name: map
inputs.doc: the surface (an elevation...)

outputs.name: map
outputs.doc: the TRI

params.name: s
params.doc: the window: odd cells, or [rows, columns] (3)

name: surface.vrm
doc: The vector ruggedness measure (spatialEco's vrm): 1 less the length of the summed unit normals of a window over its cells.

inputs.name: map
inputs.doc: the surface (an elevation...)

outputs.name: map
outputs.doc: the VRM

params.name: s
params.doc: the window: odd cells, or [rows, columns] (3)

name: surface.window
doc: Surface metrics in a moving window around every cell (landschaft's surface.window_metrics through its C++): the metrics of the window's surface at its centre, no value beyond the edges (and beyond window / 2 cells in a circle). A map per metric, in a stack.

inputs.name: map
inputs.doc: the surface

outputs.name: maps
outputs.doc: a map per metric, by its name

params.name: metrics
params.doc: names (default every one)

params.name: window
params.doc: the window's side in cells, odd, 3 or more (5)

params.name: shape
params.doc: square (default) or circle

name: swat.run
doc: Simulate a SWAT+ project (a TxtInOut folder or a zip of one) as SWAT+ 62.0.1 does, through landschaft's port of it (bit for bit with SWAT+ for what the port covers: measured and generated weather, HRUs with snow, ET, curve number runoff, MUSLE erosion, percolation, lateral flow, nutrients, plant growth and management, routing units, aquifers, SWAT-DEG channels). The tables SWAT+ prints, at a step: a row per date (year, day of the year) and object (HRU, channel, aquifer; the basin's by date).

outputs.name: weather
outputs.doc: the daily weather of each station (year, day, station)

outputs.name: hru_wb
outputs.doc: what SWAT+ prints (columns and units as its own)

outputs.name: hru_nb
outputs.doc: what SWAT+ prints (columns and units as its own)

outputs.name: hru_ls
outputs.doc: what SWAT+ prints (columns and units as its own)

outputs.name: hru_pw
outputs.doc: what SWAT+ prints (columns and units as its own)

outputs.name: basin_wb
outputs.doc: what SWAT+ prints (columns and units as its own)

outputs.name: basin_nb
outputs.doc: what SWAT+ prints (columns and units as its own)

outputs.name: basin_ls
outputs.doc: what SWAT+ prints (columns and units as its own)

outputs.name: basin_pw
outputs.doc: what SWAT+ prints (columns and units as its own)

outputs.name: channel_sd
outputs.doc: what SWAT+ prints (columns and units as its own)

outputs.name: aquifer
outputs.doc: what SWAT+ prints (columns and units as its own)

params.name: path
params.doc: the TxtInOut folder (with file.cio) or a zip of it

params.name: step
params.doc: of the tables: day, month, year (default) or aa (average annual)

params.name: tables
params.doc: the tables printed (default every one): hru_wb, hru_nb, hru_ls, hru_pw, basin_wb, basin_nb, basin_ls, basin_pw, channel_sd, aquifer

params.name: nyskip
params.doc: years simulated before printing (spin-up)

params.name: c_factor
params.doc: MUSLE's C: swatplus (default, SWAT+ 62's from APEX) or plant (the plants' minimum, SWAT+'s earlier method)

name: table.aggregate
doc: Rows grouped by the values of some columns and summarised, as dplyr's group_by and summarise: a row per group (the groups in the order of their values), its columns n (the rows in the group) and, for every column summarised and statistic, column_statistic (area_sum, area_mean). Missing values are left out of the statistics; sd is the sample's (n - 1, as R's sd). Without columns to group by, the whole table is one group.

inputs.name: table
inputs.doc: the table

outputs.name: table
outputs.doc: a row per group

params.name: by
params.doc: the columns to group by: a name, names separated by commas or a list (none: one group)

params.name: columns
params.doc: the columns summarised (default: every other)

params.name: stats
params.doc: the statistics: sum, mean, count, min, max, sd, median (default sum)

name: table.calc
doc: A column computed row by row from an expression over the others, as a spreadsheet's field calculator or dplyr's mutate: the expressions of map algebra (area / 10000, cells if class == 1 else 0), the node's other inputs as numbers by their names. A column of the same name is replaced, else it is added at the end.

inputs.name: table
inputs.doc: the table

outputs.name: table
outputs.doc: the table with the column

params.name: column
params.doc: the column's name

params.name: expression
params.doc: its value at every row, e.g. area / 10000

name: table.filter
doc: The rows of a table where an expression is true, as dplyr's filter: the columns by their names, the expressions of map algebra (class == 3 and area > 10; isnull(x) for a missing value), the node's other inputs as numbers by their names. A row where the expression is missing is left out.

inputs.name: table
inputs.doc: the table

outputs.name: table
outputs.doc: its rows where the expression is true

params.name: expression
params.doc: what a row kept is, e.g. class == 3 and area > 10

name: table.join
doc: Two tables joined by key columns, as dplyr's joins: every row of the left with each row of the right of the same key (left: the left's rows without one kept, the right's columns missing; inner: only the rows of keys in both; full: the right's rows without one added too). The right's other columns follow the left's; one of a name the left has takes a suffix.

inputs.name: left
inputs.doc: the left table

inputs.name: right
inputs.doc: the right table

outputs.name: table
outputs.doc: the tables joined

params.name: on
params.doc: the key columns, of the same names in both: a name, names separated by commas or a list

params.name: right_on
params.doc: the right's key columns, when they are named otherwise (as many as on)

params.name: how
params.doc: left, inner or full (default left)

params.name: suffix
params.doc: added to a right's column of a name the left has (default _right)

name: table.of
doc: A table written in the settings: its columns' names and its rows of numbers (null: no value), such as the small tables a planning problem takes.

outputs.name: table
outputs.doc: the table

params.name: columns
params.doc: the columns' names

params.name: rows
params.doc: the rows: [[number, ...], ...], as many numbers as columns

name: table.pivot
doc: A table from long to wide or back, as tidyr's pivot_wider and pivot_longer. Wider: a row per value of the id columns, a column per value of the names column (named prefix and the value: to_1, to_2...) holding the values column (transitions from, to, cells into a matrix). Longer: the columns given (or every column but the id ones) into rows of two columns, the names and the values; a table's values being numbers, the name of a column is the number in it (2011 of y2011 with prefix y; 1 of to_1), else its place among them (1, 2...).

inputs.name: table
inputs.doc: the table

outputs.name: table
outputs.doc: the table pivoted

params.name: direction
params.doc: wider or longer

params.name: id
params.doc: the columns that make a row (wider), or kept as they are (longer)

params.name: names
params.doc: wider: the column whose values become columns

params.name: values
params.doc: wider: the column whose values fill them

params.name: prefix
params.doc: the new columns' names before the value (wider), or before the number in the names (longer) (default: the names column's name and _)

params.name: fill
params.doc: wider: the value of a combination absent (default none)

params.name: columns
params.doc: longer: the columns turned into rows (default every one but the id ones)

params.name: names_to
params.doc: longer: the column of the names (default name)

params.name: values_to
params.doc: longer: the column of the values (default value)

name: table.read
doc: A table from a file: comma-separated values (.csv), tab-separated (.tsv, .txt), with ; as Excel writes them where a comma marks the decimals (the separator and the decimal mark found by themselves), or JSON (.json, a list of rows). A header names the columns; an empty value, or NA, is none. The columns of text (names, not numbers) are left out: a table is of numbers.

outputs.name: table
outputs.doc: the table

params.name: path
params.doc: the file, relative to the model's folder

params.name: separator
params.doc: between the values: , ; or tab (default: found)

params.name: decimal
params.doc: the decimal mark: . or , (default: found)

name: table.select
doc: Columns of a table chosen (in the order given), left out, or renamed, as dplyr's select and rename.

inputs.name: table
inputs.doc: the table

outputs.name: table
outputs.doc: its columns chosen

params.name: columns
params.doc: the columns kept, in this order (default every one)

params.name: drop
params.doc: the columns left out

params.name: rename
params.doc: new names: { old = "new", ... }

name: table.sort
doc: The rows of a table sorted by some columns (the first, then the next where it ties; missing values last), as dplyr's arrange, and the first rows kept (top: the ten largest patches, say).

inputs.name: table
inputs.doc: the table

outputs.name: table
outputs.doc: its rows sorted

params.name: by
params.doc: the columns to sort by: a name, names separated by commas or a list

params.name: descending
params.doc: from the largest (default false)

params.name: top
params.doc: the first rows kept (default every row)

name: table.write
doc: Write a table to a file, its format by the extension: comma-separated values (.csv, the default), tab-separated (.tsv, .txt) or JSON (.json, a list of rows); a value missing is left empty (null in JSON). For a spreadsheet that reads a comma as the decimal mark: separator ; and decimal ,.

inputs.name: table
inputs.doc: the table

outputs.name: path
outputs.doc: the file written

params.name: path
params.doc: the file, relative to the model's folder

params.name: separator
params.doc: between the values: , ; or tab (default by the extension)

params.name: decimal
params.doc: the decimal mark: . (default) or ,

name: uncertainty.delta
doc: The uncertainty of an expression of the node's maps and numbers (raster.calc's) from the uncertainty of its parameters, by the delta method (landschaft's delta_method, the GUM's first order): the derivatives by finite differences (central, or forward as Strassburg et al. 2020), the standard deviation sqrt(sum (df/dp sigma)^2) (quadratic) or sum |df/dp sigma| (linear).

outputs.name: value
outputs.doc: the expression at the parameters (a map or a number)

outputs.name: sd
outputs.doc: its standard deviation

params.name: expression
params.doc: e.g. carbon * factor + base

params.name: parameters
params.doc: [["factor", 0.47, 0.02], ...]: name, value, sd

params.name: method
params.doc: quadratic (default) or linear

params.name: scheme
params.doc: central (default) or forward

params.name: step
params.doc: the finite-difference step (one, or one per parameter)

name: uncertainty.interval
doc: The normal confidence interval of a value: value -/+ z sd, z the normal quantile of the level (landschaft's interval; scipy's norm.ppf, cephes' ndtri; Strassburg et al. 2020 fix z at 1.96).

inputs.name: value
inputs.doc: a map or a number

inputs.name: sd
inputs.doc: its standard deviation

outputs.name: low
outputs.doc: the lower bound

outputs.name: high
outputs.doc: the upper bound

params.name: level
params.doc: the confidence level, 0 to 1 (0.95)

name: uncertainty.monte_carlo
doc: The uncertainty of an expression of the node's maps and numbers by drawing its parameters (landschaft's monte_carlo): n draws from normal distributions with numpy's generator and seed, the expression computed for each, their mean, standard deviation and quantiles (numpy's).

outputs.name: mean
outputs.doc: the mean over the draws (a map or a number)

outputs.name: sd
outputs.doc: the standard deviation over the draws

outputs.name: quantiles
outputs.doc: a layer (or a row) per quantile

params.name: expression
params.doc: e.g. carbon * factor + base

params.name: parameters
params.doc: [["factor", 0.47, 0.02], ...]: name, mean, sd

params.name: n
params.doc: the draws (1000)

params.name: seed
params.doc: of numpy's generator (0)

name: uncertainty.product_sd
doc: The standard deviation of the product of two independent uncertain values x v (landschaft's product_sd): Goodman's exact variance x^2 sigma_v^2 + v^2 sigma_x^2 + sigma_x^2 sigma_v^2, cell by cell, or of the sum of the products (total: quadratic or linear).

inputs.name: x
inputs.doc: a map or a number

inputs.name: sd_x
inputs.doc: its standard deviation

inputs.name: v
inputs.doc: a map or a number

inputs.name: sd_v
inputs.doc: its standard deviation

outputs.name: sd
outputs.doc: a map (or a number) of standard deviations, or the total's

params.name: total
params.doc: the standard deviation of the sum of the products

params.name: method
params.doc: of the total: quadratic (default) or linear

name: uncertainty.sum_sd
doc: The standard deviation of a total of uncertain values, the sum of w v (landschaft's sum_sd): independent errors sqrt(sum (sigma w)^2), errors adding up sum |sigma w|, or with a correlation rho of every pair sqrt((1 - rho) sum s^2 + rho (sum s)^2). Missing cells left out.

inputs.name: sd
inputs.doc: the values' standard deviations

inputs.name: weights
inputs.doc: a map or a number (default 1)

outputs.name: sd
outputs.doc: the total's standard deviation

params.name: method
params.doc: quadratic (default) or linear

params.name: correlation
params.doc: of every pair of errors, -1 to 1

name: validate.agreement
doc: How a simulated map matches the observed one, both from the same start: the share of cells of the same class, the figure of merit (hits / (hits + misses + false alarms + wrong hits)) and its terms.

inputs.name: start
inputs.doc: the map both start from

inputs.name: observed
inputs.doc: the observed map

inputs.name: simulated
inputs.doc: the simulated map

outputs.name: table
outputs.doc: overall, figure_of_merit, hits, misses, false_alarms, wrong_hits

name: validate.error_budget
doc: MOLUSCE's error budget (Pontius 2002, through landschaft): the agreement of the maps when the simulation has no, medium or perfect information of quantity and location, at the maps' resolution and coarser ones, merging scale x scale cells each time (the edges left over dropped).

inputs.name: reference
inputs.doc: the reference map

inputs.name: simulated
inputs.doc: the simulated map (no classes the reference lacks)

outputs.name: table
outputs.doc: per resolution: cells, no_no, no_medium, medium_medium, medium_perfect, perfect_perfect

params.name: iterations
params.doc: the resolutions (default 3)

params.name: scale
params.doc: cells merged per side each time (default 2)

name: validate.futures
doc: FUTURES' validation (r.futures.validation through landschaft): the quantity and allocation disagreement per class and in total (Pontius & Millones 2011) and kappa; with the original map, kappa simulation (van Vliet et al. 2011) and, for 0/1 maps, misses, hits, false alarms, null successes, the figure of merit, producer's and user's accuracy (Pontius et al. 2008).

inputs.name: reference
inputs.doc: the observed map (integer classes)

inputs.name: simulated
inputs.doc: the simulated map

inputs.name: original
inputs.doc: the map at the start

outputs.name: metrics
outputs.doc: the scalar metrics (empty where they cannot be computed)

outputs.name: classes
outputs.doc: per class: quantity and allocation disagreement

name: validate.futures_grid
doc: FUTURES' validation per tile or per region (r.futures.gridvalidation through landschaft): a row per tile of size x size cells from the top-left (its row, column and centre) or per region, the metrics of validate.futures and the cells compared.

inputs.name: reference
inputs.doc: the observed map (integer classes)

inputs.name: simulated
inputs.doc: the simulated map

inputs.name: original
inputs.doc: the map at the start

inputs.name: regions
inputs.doc: region ids, in place of tiles

outputs.name: table
outputs.doc: per tile or region: where, cells, the metrics

params.name: size
params.doc: the tiles' side in cells

name: validate.kappa
doc: MOLUSCE's comparison of two maps of classes (DependenceCoef through landschaft): kappa, kappa location and kappa histogram and the % of cells of the same class over the classes of both maps; Cramer's V and the joint information uncertainty; the correlation of the class values.

inputs.name: reference
inputs.doc: the reference map

inputs.name: simulated
inputs.doc: the simulated map

outputs.name: table
outputs.doc: kappa, kappa_location, kappa_histogram, correctness, cramer, jiu, correlation

name: validate.similarity
doc: Dinamica EGO's validation: the fuzzy similarity of the simulated and the observed change (the cells that changed from the start, in their new class) in windows of growing size; the minimum of the two directions is Dinamica's result.

inputs.name: start
inputs.doc: the map both start from

inputs.name: observed
inputs.doc: the observed map

inputs.name: simulated
inputs.doc: the simulated map

outputs.name: table
outputs.doc: a row per window

params.name: windows
params.doc: the window sides, odd ([1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11])

params.name: decay
params.doc: "exponential" (default) or "constant"

name: validate.three_map
doc: The three-map comparison of a simulation (Pontius, Peethambaram & Castella 2011; lulcc's ThreeMapComparison through landschaft): the reference at the start and at the end and the simulated end compared at blocks of several sizes, the budget of agreement and disagreement (misses, hits, wrong hits, false alarms, correct rejections; overall, per class, per transition) and the figure of merit. The cells without a value in any map are left out of all three.

inputs.name: t0
inputs.doc: the reference map at the start

inputs.name: t1
inputs.doc: the reference map at the end

inputs.name: simulated
inputs.doc: the simulated map of the end

outputs.name: table
outputs.doc: per factor lulcc's table: t0 class within t1 class (empty: total), the simulated classes, total

outputs.name: budget
outputs.doc: level (0 overall, 1 class, 2 transition), from, to, factor, misses, hits, wrong_hits, false_alarms, correct_rejections

outputs.name: figure_of_merit
outputs.doc: per factor: overall, then per class

outputs.name: transitions
outputs.doc: per factor and class from: the figure of merit to each

params.name: factors
params.doc: the blocks' sides in cells (default [1])

params.name: categories
params.doc: the classes (default those of the maps)

name: value.calc
doc: A number or a text from the node's inputs, not a map: `expression` in map algebra's syntax and functions over the inputs that are numbers (true and false as 1 and 0), a table's value as table.column (of the row `row`); `text` a template of the inputs, {name} replaced by each one's value ({value} by the expression's): the path a loop writes (out/{species}_{year}.tif), the number a setting reads, the case of a switch.

outputs.name: value
outputs.doc: the expression's value

outputs.name: text
outputs.doc: the text

params.name: expression
params.doc: e.g. area / 10000, 0.3 if year < 2010 else 0.5

params.name: text
params.doc: e.g. out/{species}_{year}.tif

params.name: row
params.doc: the row of the tables read (1 the first, -1 the last; 1)

name: vector.buffer
doc: The area within a distance of every feature (GEOS through GDAL, as shapely's buffer): circles around points, corridors along lines, polygons grown (or shrunk, with a negative distance); the features' attributes kept, or every buffer merged into one (dissolve).

inputs.name: vector
inputs.doc: the features

outputs.name: vector
outputs.doc: the buffers

params.name: distance
params.doc: the distance, in the features' units

params.name: segments
params.doc: segments of a quarter circle (16)

params.name: dissolve
params.doc: merge the buffers into one feature (false)

name: vector.calc
doc: Attributes computed for every feature from a script over the others, as QGIS's field calculator, in map algebra's language (Python's syntax): the attributes by their names (the characters other than letters, digits and _ as _: individual-local-identifier as individual_local_identifier), numbers and texts ("high" if pop > 100 else "low"; uso == "forest"; float(code) reads a text as a number), the geometry's measures (geometry.area, geometry.perimeter, geometry.length, geometry.x, geometry.y), feature (the number 1..), x.sum() and the other methods over all the features, the node's other inputs (numbers and texts) by their names. One statement a line (# a comment): name = value, name[where] = value, and out name = value (or out name) for each attribute given; without out, the last value is the attribute `column`. An attribute of the same name is replaced, else it is added.

inputs.name: vector
inputs.doc: the features

outputs.name: vector
outputs.doc: the features with the attributes

outputs.name: table
outputs.doc: their attributes

params.name: column
params.doc: the attribute's name (a script without out)

params.name: expression
params.doc: its value, e.g. geometry.area / 10000; or a script: density = pop / geometry.area; out dense = density > 100

name: vector.clip
doc: Features cut to the area of a mask (the union of its polygons; GEOS through GDAL, as geopandas' clip): each feature's part inside it, those outside it left out, their attributes kept.

inputs.name: vector
inputs.doc: the features

inputs.name: mask
inputs.doc: the polygons they are cut to (reprojected to them)

outputs.name: vector
outputs.doc: the features' parts inside the mask

name: vector.density
doc: The density of points on a map's grid, as ArcGIS's Kernel Density or QGIS's Heatmap: each point (its weight an attribute, or 1) spread by a kernel over a radius, the kernel's integral the weight, so the map is points per square map unit (or per hectare, per km²); quartic (biweight, the default, ArcGIS's), triweight, Epanechnikov, triangular or uniform; or the points in each cell counted (count; with a field, their sum). Without a radius ArcGIS's default (Silverman's rule). The points are reprojected to the map; distances in its units (a map in metres for densities per area).

inputs.name: vector
inputs.doc: the points

inputs.name: map
inputs.doc: a map on whose grid the density is made

outputs.name: map
outputs.doc: the density (or count) of every cell

params.name: kernel
params.doc: quartic (default), triweight, epanechnikov, triangular, uniform or count

params.name: radius
params.doc: the kernel's radius in map units (Silverman's rule)

params.name: field
params.doc: the attribute weighting each point (none: 1)

params.name: units
params.doc: per square map unit (default), per hectare or per km²

name: vector.dissolve
doc: Features merged (GEOS's union through GDAL, as geopandas' dissolve): all into one, or one per value of an attribute (`by`), with that value and the features merged (count).

inputs.name: vector
inputs.doc: the features (of one kind: points, lines or polygons)

outputs.name: vector
outputs.doc: the features merged

params.name: by
params.doc: the attribute whose values are merged apart (none: all)

name: vector.distance
doc: The distance (in the map's units) from every cell's centre to the nearest cell of the features (as vector.rasterize burns them), exactly (the Euclidean distance transform). Out of core (block_rows, a path, or rasters on disk of more than 250 million cells) by strips into a GeoTIFF, the same distances (but where GDAL draws a line through cells' corners with all_touched).

inputs.name: vector
inputs.doc: the features

inputs.name: like
inputs.doc: a map on the grid of the distances (only its grid is read)

outputs.name: map
outputs.doc: the distance of every cell (0 in the features; on disk for rasters on disk)

params.name: all_touched
params.doc: every cell a feature touches is one (false)

params.name: block_rows
params.doc: out of core: by strips of this many rows into a GeoTIFF (path); on the grid of rasters on disk of more than 250 million cells always

params.name: path
params.doc: out of core: the GeoTIFF written (default next to the rasters: name_distance.tif)

name: vector.exact_sum
doc: The coverage-weighted sum of a map (or of every layer of a stack) over every polygon, exactextractr's exact_extract(fun = "sum"): every cell weighted by the share of it the polygon covers, exactly (the amounts of features in planning units of polygons). Out of core (block_rows, or rasters on disk of more than 250 million cells) the windows under every polygon read from disk, the same sums.

name: vector.extract
doc: The values of a map (or of every layer of a stack) at points, landschaft's extract: the cell holding each point (nearest) or interpolated from the four nearest cell centres (bilinear, the weights over those with a value); with a buffer, the statistics of the cells within that radius of each point (zonal_stats of GEOS's circles). name: vector.filter
doc: The features where an expression over their attributes is true, as QGIS's Select by Expression or geopandas' query, in map algebra's language (Python's syntax): the attributes by their names (the characters other than letters, digits and _ as _: individual-local-identifier as individual_local_identifier), numbers and texts (area > 10000 and uso == "forest"; float(code) reads a text as a number), the geometry's measures (geometry.area, geometry.perimeter, geometry.length, geometry.x, geometry.y), feature (the number 1..), the node's other inputs (numbers and texts) by their names. A script of several lines gives names values (density = pop / geometry.area) and ends with the condition. A feature where it is missing is left out.
